## Question

How do NFL Combine performance measures differ across player positions, and which positions tend to have the fastest 40-yard dash times and highest vertical jumps?

## Main figure

```{r}
#| label: main-figure
#| eval: false
library(tidyverse)

my_data <- read_csv("../data/tidy/your_file.csv")
# Your ggplot code here; add fig-cap and fig-alt
```

## What it shows

The figure shows a negative relationship between 40-yard dash time and vertical jump height. Positions such as wide receivers (WR), running backs (RB), and cornerbacks (CB) generally have faster dash times and higher vertical jumps, while offensive linemen tend to have slower dash times and lower vertical jumps. The position centers summarize the average performance for each group.

## Limitations

The data come from an NFL Combine dataset, with one row representing one player. Some positions have fewer players than others, so averages for smaller groups may be less reliable. The data cannot tell us why positions differ, whether training caused the differences, or how combine performance translates to success in NFL games.
